method: Deep Georgian PDO pass. Exact product specifications are separated from registry identity. Analytical, viticultural and process rules are retained as published; ambiguous translated fields remain notes rather than silently normalized.

profiles.name: Kisi Magraani

productionRules.grapeComposition: 100% Kisi (specification synonym: Kisi Magraani); other varieties prohibited

white.fermentation: grape juice/free-run after pressing and sedimentation
white.mustMaceration: permitted before fermentation and/or at the beginning

amber.postFermentationSkinContactUntil: 1 February of the year following harvest

terroir.aspect: southern and south-western Caucasus Range slopes
terroir.climate: moderately continental and comparatively humid, with hot summers and long cold winters

styleNotes: Official specification describes young white wine with meadow-flower, apple, pear, peach and citrus tones and aged white with dry-grass/dried-fruit development.
Official specification describes young amber wine with apple, pear and peach, developing almond and dried-apricot notes with age.
researchNotes: The specification records a local survival history for Kisi Magraani and states that low yield limited its spread during the communist period.
The specification records 1940s scientific-institute work distinguishing the Magraani form; this historical statement is preserved as source history, not genetic proof of a distinct cultivar.

profiles.name: Khvanchkara

terroir.setting: slopes on both sides of the Rioni in Racha
terroir.geologyAndTextureNote: the PDO specification differentiates six soil variants by village rather than one generic Khvanchkara soil

styleNotes: red, naturally semi-sweet; official product specification describes a fine, velvety style tied to Aleksandrouli and Mujuretuli and local conditions
historicalNotes: The specification traces Kipiani Wine to the 1870s and records the name Khvanchkara from 1930.
The specification states that before 1942 the local semi-sweet production lacked modern stabilization and fermentation could stop in autumn/winter cold and restart with spring warmth.
researchNotes: The English specification contains an ambiguous translated acidity line; it is intentionally not normalized into a volatile-acidity maximum without a clearer legal text.
